research_question: For sparse categorical CTR/ranking data with only ~5 low-cardinality fields (user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, duration-bucket), is Field-aware Factorization Machines (FFM) — where each feature has a separate latent vector per *interacting field* rather than one shared embedding — established to reliably outperform plain FM on ranking quality (not just LogLoss/AUC on pointwise CTR benchmarks), and is there a cheap way to keep the field-specific embedding blowup (normally O(num_fields^2 x k) parameters) CPU-tractable with only 5 fields inside a BPR pairwise training loop, e.g. by only field-aware-izing the two highest-cardinality fields (user_id, video_id) and keeping the rest shared?
reflection: The k-sweep confirmed the plateau is not a raw capacity ceiling (k=8 tied k=16, k=32/64 slightly worse from overfitting) — order-2 FM's expressiveness itself, not its embedding width, is the bottleneck, and the earlier DeepFM MLP-branch attempt to add higher-order capacity also failed by overfitting fast. Per the plateau warning, before guessing another variant of the same order-2-FM-plus-BPR mechanism I should check whether a different, specifically CTR-proven interaction structure (rather than a bolted-on MLP) is the right lever.

note.title: FFM vs FM for ranking; field-weighted FM as cheap alternative to full field-awareness
note.citation: Pan et al. 2018, WWW ("Field-weighted Factorization Machines"); cf. Juan et al. 2016, RecSys ("Field-aware Factorization Machines for CTR Prediction")
note.tags: FFM, FM, FwFM, field-aware factorization machine, BPR, pairwise ranking, CTR, parameter efficiency, sparse categorical features, KuaiRand, embedding blowup
note.body: FFM's advantage over plain FM (Juan et al. 2016) was established on pointwise CTR benchmarks (Criteo/Avazu, LogLoss/AUC) with dozens of fields; I found no reliable, citable evidence that FFM reliably beats FM on ranking-quality metrics (NDCG/Recall@K) under a pairwise BPR loss, and with only ~5 low-cardinality fields the field-interaction diversity that gives FFM its edge is much smaller anyway, so gains are not established for your setting. FFM's cost is O(n²k) field-specific embedding tables (n=fields, k=latent dim) per feature value, which is what causes the blowup — with only 5 fields this is a manageable 25 sub-vectors per feature-value in principle, but still 5x the memory of FM per high-cardinality feature (user_id, video_id, author_id) if done naively for every field pair. The cheap, literature-backed fix is not "make 2 fields field-aware and leave the rest shared" (I could not find that specific ablation validated anywhere) but Field-weighted FM (FwFM, Pan et al. 2018, WWW): keep one shared embedding per feature (like FM) and add a single learned scalar weight r_{F(i),F(j)} per field-pair to modulate the interaction strength, reproducing ~FFM-level accuracy with as little as ~4% of FFM's parameters and O(n²) extra scalars instead of O(n²k) extra vectors. A related paper, FM² (Field-matrixed FM, arXiv:2102.12994), similarly reduces cost via low-rank field-interaction matrices rather than full per-field embeddings, and is a reasonable named alternative to mention. Given the weak evidence for FFM's benefit here plus the small field count, FwFM (or plain FM) inside your BPR loop is the safer, CPU-tractable choice; the specific "field-aware only user_id/video_id" heuristic is a plausible engineering shortcut in the spirit of FwFM/FM² but should be treated as an untested ad hoc idea, not an established method.
